title: Schindler's List
synopsis: Kraków, 1939. You're a German businessman with a gift for getting on the right side of every officer at every party. The Jews of this city are about to need a list with your name on it.

nodes.text: Officers, cognac, jazz. You buy every round. Both choices lead to The Factory, but “Make a connection” arrives there with a different cost than “Buy more rounds.” By The Factory, the decision will already have changed who trusts you.

choices.consequence: You choose to make a connection. It opens the route to The Factory, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You buy more rounds. The decision moves you toward The Factory and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: An enamelware factory, abandoned. A man named Stern keeps the books. The road still runs toward Jewish Workers. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Hire Stern” and choosing “Hire a German.” At Jewish Workers, the people waiting will read the choice before the explanation.

choices.consequence: You hire Stern. The decision moves you toward Jewish Workers and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You choose to hire a German. It opens the route to Jewish Workers, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Cheap labor, the regime says. People, you see, when you look at them. You cannot avoid Goeth; you can only decide whether “Hire many” or “Hire few” defines the person who reaches it. In Jewish Workers, waiting would only let someone else define what your silence meant.

choices.consequence: You choose to hire many. It opens the route to Goeth, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You hire few. The decision moves you toward Goeth and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Camp commandant. Cruel. Charming when useful. Helen Hirsch is already waiting. What changes is whether “Befriend him” or “Avoid him” is the instinct you carry into it. In Goeth, waiting would only let someone else define what your silence meant.

choices.consequence: You commit to befriend him. By Helen Hirsch, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You choose to avoid him. It opens the route to Helen Hirsch, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Goeth's maid. He beats her. You bring her medicine quietly. The Ghetto is already waiting. What changes is whether “Help quietly” or “Confront Goeth” is the instinct you carry into it. At The Ghetto, the people waiting will read the choice before the explanation.

choices.consequence: You commit to help quietly. By The Ghetto, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You commit to confront Goeth. By The Ghetto, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: Liquidation day. The streets fill with bodies and shoes. A girl in a red coat. Stern's Lists is already waiting. What changes is whether “Watch from the hill” or “Look away” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You commit to watch from the hill. By Stern's Lists, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You commit to look away. By Stern's Lists, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: Stern brings names. Each name is a person. Each person is a deduction from your factory's price. The road still runs toward Payoffs. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Approve every name” and choosing “Cap the list.”

choices.consequence: You approve every name. The decision moves you toward Payoffs and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You cap the list. The decision moves you toward Payoffs and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: You buy people one bribe at a time. The price changes weekly. Both choices lead to Goeth's Pardons, but “Pay it” arrives there with a different cost than “Negotiate.” By Goeth's Pardons, the decision will already have changed who trusts you.

choices.consequence: You pay it. The decision moves you toward Goeth's Pardons and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You negotiate. The decision moves you toward Goeth's Pardons and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: You convince Goeth to grant pardons for sport. He likes the idea of being god. You cannot avoid The Wedding; you can only decide whether “Encourage it” or “Disgust him” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You choose to encourage it. It opens the route to The Wedding, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You disgust him. The decision moves you toward The Wedding and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: A Jewish wedding in the camp. You attend secretly. Auschwitz Train is already waiting. What changes is whether “Drink” or “Stand far back” is the instinct you carry into it. In The Wedding, waiting would only let someone else define what your silence meant.

choices.consequence: You choose to drink. It opens the route to Auschwitz Train, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You stand far back. The decision moves you toward Auschwitz Train and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: A train of your women workers is misrouted to Auschwitz. Both choices lead to Auschwitz Office, but “Buy them back” arrives there with a different cost than “Send a telegram first.” In Auschwitz Train, waiting would only let someone else define what your silence meant.

choices.consequence: You commit to buy them back. By Auschwitz Office, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You send a telegram first. The decision moves you toward Auschwitz Office and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: You enter the office with a diamond brooch and a smile. Women Returned is already waiting. What changes is whether “Smile larger” or “Show the diamond first” is the instinct you carry into it. In Auschwitz Office, waiting would only let someone else define what your silence meant.

choices.consequence: You commit to smile larger. By Women Returned, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You commit to show the diamond first. By Women Returned, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: The women come back. The relief is private. The road still runs toward The List. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Hide the relief” and choosing “Show some warmth.” At The List, the people waiting will read the choice before the explanation.

choices.consequence: You commit to hide the relief. By The List, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You commit to show some warmth. By The List, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: Stern, at the typewriter. Names. More names. Eleven hundred names. Both choices lead to Final Bribes, but “Add every Stern suggests” arrives there with a different cost than “Add a few you've thought of.” In The List, waiting would only let someone else define what your silence meant.

choices.consequence: You choose to add every Stern suggests. It opens the route to Final Bribes, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Add a few you've thought of
choices.consequence: You choose to add a few you've thought of. It opens the route to Final Bribes, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Your fortune is, by now, mostly gone. Each name has cost a price. The road still runs toward The Workers Arrive. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Spend the rest” and choosing “Save a little.”

choices.consequence: You spend the rest. The decision moves you toward The Workers Arrive and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You choose to save a little. It opens the route to The Workers Arrive, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: The eleven hundred arrive at Brünnlitz. They are, for now, alive. The Last Months is already waiting. What changes is whether “Be at the gate” or “Stay in the office” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You choose to be at the gate. It opens the route to The Last Months, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You choose to stay in the office. It opens the route to The Last Months, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: You make worthless ammunition on purpose. The war ends in slow degrees. You cannot avoid Liberation; you can only decide whether “Keep faking” or “Risk less” defines the person who reaches it. At Liberation, the people waiting will read the choice before the explanation.

choices.consequence: You keep faking. The decision moves you toward Liberation and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You commit to risk less. By Liberation, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: A Russian officer rides in. The workers are no longer prisoners. The Ring is already waiting. What changes is whether “Speak to them” or “Stand to the side” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You choose to speak to them. It opens the route to The Ring, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You stand to the side. The decision moves you toward The Ring and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: The workers melt down their gold to make you a ring. He who saves one life. Could Have Saved More is already waiting. What changes is whether “Take the ring” or “Refuse” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You commit to take the ring. By Could Have Saved More, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You commit to refuse. By Could Have Saved More, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: You break, in front of Stern, over the car you could have sold, the pin you could have sold. Years Later comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Let it out” and “Bury it.”

choices.consequence: You choose to let it out. It opens the route to Years Later, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
You bury it. The decision moves you toward Years Later and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: You die a poor man, honored. The workers and their children visit your grave for decades. “Be remembered” draws you toward He Who Saves One Life; “Be forgotten quietly” leaves Stern's Friendship waiting on the other side. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Helen, Free in play.

choices.consequence: You be remembered. The decision moves you toward He Who Saves One Life and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You be forgotten quietly. The decision moves you toward Stern's Friendship and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You choose to take the third path. It opens the route to Helen, Free, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: The ring is, in the end, the only inheritance you wanted to leave. The descendants of the eleven hundred number, by the time you are remembered, more than the population of Kraków. The road into He Who Saves One Life began with “Be remembered” in Years Later; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

Stern survives you. He writes the list down again, properly, with photographs. The list, in libraries, becomes a kind of scripture. The road into Stern's Friendship began with “Be forgotten quietly” in Years Later; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

Helen survives. She emigrates. Years later she sits at a kitchen table with your widow, drinking coffee, talking about a man neither of them could have predicted. The road into Helen, Free began with “Take the third path” in Years Later; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
